newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah stable in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah stable in late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah fell against the dollar on Monday on fears of more election campaign violence but was stable in active late trading, dealers said.
One Japanese bank dealer said the market was quite active, with plenty of sellers and buyers on both side.
"It appears to be a comfortable level for dollar sellers to cash out with good levels for players to come in," he said.

Dealers said the rupiah hovered between 2,442.0 and 2,445.0, with the underlying tone seen favouring the dollar because of the election campaign. Spot rupiah was at 2,442.5/43.5 at 0830 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,438/0/40.0.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,442.25/43.00 and 2,440.50/41.00, respectively.

One U.S. bank dealer said there were some dollar purchases by Tokyo and Singapore investors this morning in response to weekend violence in Jakarta, but the market seemed to have largely discounted the factor.
He said initial dollar buying was sporadic only, with strong counter selling from local players capping the upside.
"Local players have gone long earlier heavily. They don't have any problem to cash out now," the dealer said.
He said offshore players were surprised by the cool local response to the weekend violence, prompting them to slow down.

On Saturday and Sunday, clashes between supporters of the ruling Golkar party and loyalists of the minority United Development Party (PPP) broke out in various parts of the capital of 10 million people.
Newspapers also said there was sporadic violence on Sunday in the ancient city of Yogyakarta and the nearby town of Bantul, but there were no injuries or arrests.
Jakarta police said the situation was under control. There were no reports of arrests or injuries.
But the dealer said further softening of the rupiah was likely this week because of investors going long on dollars ahead of public holidays in Singapore on Wednesday and in Jakarta on Thursday.
Dealers said liquidity was ample in the afternoon, which had helped support the dollar. Overnight money fell to seven percent from 14.0/15.0 percent in the morning.
Overnight swap was at 0.4/0.5 and tom/next at 0.25/0.30.
They said the spread of swap points was narrowing, suggesting the market was stabilising after last week's spillover from Thailand's woes and campaign jitters.
One-month swap was at 21.0/22.0, two at 33.5/36.5, three at 49.0/50.0 and six at 92.0/97.0.
The central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,410/2,602 and raised its conversion band by nine points to 2,418/2,466 on Monday. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
